findings.title: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses logical AND (`&&`) instead of OR (`||`)
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Using `&&` requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously. A team admin who is not an owner (or any user if `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` check mutually exclusive roles) will evaluate to `false` and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when trying to add guests to a team booking. This should use `||`.

findings.title: `EventManager` is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` permits team admins/owners and existing attendees—not just the booking organizer—to add guests. However, lines 158–165 fetch credentials for `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) and construct `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` with the caller's user object rather than the booking organizer (`booking.user`, whose `credentials` and `destinationCalendar` were fetched in the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` query at lines 35–40 but never used). When a team admin/owner or attendee adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will lack the organizer's calendar credentials and fail to update the calendar event.

findings.title: Case-sensitive email checks allow blacklist bypass and duplicate attendees
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` lowercases each configured address (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares against the raw `guest` string without lowercasing it, so any email containing uppercase characters bypasses the blacklist. Likewise, `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is case-sensitive, and neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor `uniqueGuests` deduplicates the `guests` array itself, allowing duplicate attendee records to be created if duplicate or differently cased emails are submitted to the endpoint.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is passed unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw `guests` input array rather than `uniqueGuests`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides whether an attendee receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (intended only for newly added guests) or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (intended for existing attendees). If the submitted `guests` list includes an existing attendee's email alongside a new guest, that existing attendee will be sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type settings that disable standard host/attendee emails
findings.body: Unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`, and `sendRescheduledEmails` in `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. When an event type has standard host or attendee emails disabled in its metadata, adding guests will still send notification emails.

findings.title: Validation error state `isInvalidEmail` is not cleared on valid submit or dialog close
findings.body: When email validation fails in `handleAdd`, `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called, but `isInvalidEmail` is never reset to `false` when validation passes, in `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`, or when the dialog is dismissed via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking the close icon, pressing Escape, or clicking the backdrop). Once a user triggers a validation error, the error message remains visible even after reopening the dialog, and closing the dialog without clicking the Cancel button also leaves stale entries in `multiEmailValue`.
